title: Grothendieck Ring K₀(Var): Motivic Infrastructure
content: Sets up the algebraic environment by defining `K0Var k` as a structure bundling a commutative ring `carrier` and a distinguished element `L` (the Lefschetz motive [A¹]). Derived constructions: `affineClass n = L^n` (the class [Aⁿ]), `projectiveClass n = 1 + L + ... + Lⁿ` (the class [Pⁿ]), `triangular n = n(n-1)/2`, `GLnClass n = ∏(Lⁱ - 1) · L^{T(n)}`, and `completeFlagClass n = ∏ [Pⁱ]`. These replicate and extend the setup from `MotivicFlagMaps.lean`, the parent proof.
mathContext: The **Grothendieck ring of varieties** $K_0(\text{Var}_k)$ is generated by isomorphism classes $[X]$ of varieties with $[X] = [U] + [Z]$ for $Z \hookrightarrow X$ closed, $U$ the complement. The **Lefschetz motive** $\mathbb{L} = [\mathbb{A}^1]$ generates a polynomial subring $\mathbb{Z}[\mathbb{L}] \subset K_0(\text{Var}_k)$. A key formula: $[\mathrm{GL}_n] = \prod_{i=1}^n (\mathbb{L}^i - 1) \cdot \mathbb{L}^{n(n-1)/2}$, which counts invertible matrices by the flag-counting argument.

title: q-Number [n]_L = 1 + L + ... + L^{n-1}: The Motivic Integer
content: Defines `qNumber K n = ∑_{i<n} L^i`, the q-analog of the integer n. Proved: [0]_L = 0, [1]_L = 1, [2]_L = 1 + L, and the key identity `qNumber K (n+1) = projectiveClass K n`. This last identity is the bridge between combinatorics and geometry: the q-integer [n+1]_L equals the motivic class of projective n-space [P^n]. At L = 1 (which corresponds to counting points over F₁), [n]_L reduces to the ordinary integer n.
mathContext: The **q-number** $[n]_q = 1 + q + q^2 + \cdots + q^{n-1} = \frac{q^n - 1}{q - 1}$ is the basic building block of q-combinatorics. In $K_0(\text{Var}_k)$ with $q = \mathbb{L}$: $[n]_{\mathbb{L}} = [\mathbb{P}^{n-1}]$. This encodes the **Schubert cell decomposition** of projective space: $\mathbb{P}^{n-1} = \mathbb{A}^0 \sqcup \mathbb{A}^1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup \mathbb{A}^{n-1}$, giving $[\mathbb{P}^{n-1}] = 1 + \mathbb{L} + \cdots + \mathbb{L}^{n-1}$.
prerequisites: L^i notation for Lefschetz motive powers

title: q-Factorial = Flag Variety Class: The Central Bridge
content: Defines `qFactorial K n = ∏_{i=1}^n [i]_L` and proves `qFactorial_eq_completeFlagClass`: [n]_L! = [Fl_n]. The proof is one line: `completeFlagClass n = ∏ [P^i] = ∏ qNumber (i+1) = qFactorial`. Small cases verified: [0]! = 1, [1]! = 1, [2]! = 1 + L = [P¹], [3]! = (1+L)(1+L+L²) = [P¹]·[P²]. This identity is the foundation of the Gaussian binomial theory: it says the complete flag variety [Fl_n] decomposes as a q-factorial product, mirroring how n! counts permutations of n elements.
mathContext: The identity $[n]_{\mathbb{L}}! = [\mathrm{Fl}_n]$ reflects the **tower of fibrations** $\mathrm{Fl}_n \to \mathrm{Fl}_{n-1}$ with fiber $\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$: each step adds one new hyperplane to the flag, with $[n-1]$ choices (identified with $\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$). The product formula $[\mathrm{Fl}_n] = \prod_{i=0}^{n-1} [\mathbb{P}^i]$ follows by induction on this tower.

title: Grassmannian Motivic Class via q-Pascal Recursion
content: Defines `grassmannianClass K d n` by structural recursion encoding the **q-Pascal identity**: [Gr(d+1, n+2)] = L^{d+1} · [Gr(d+1, n+1)] + [Gr(d, n+1)]. Base cases: [Gr(0,n)] = 1, [Gr(d+1,0)] = 0, [Gr(d,d)] = 1. Also directly verified: [Gr(1,2)] = 1+L, [Gr(1,3)] = 1+L+L², [Gr(2,3)] = 1+L+L², [Gr(2,4)] = 1+L+2L²+L³+L⁴. The coefficient 2 in [Gr(2,4)] on L² reflects the two Schubert cells of dimension 2: Young diagrams (2,0) and (1,1) in a 2×2 box.
mathContext: The **Gaussian binomial coefficient** $\binom{n}{d}_{\mathbb{L}} = [\mathrm{Gr}(d,n)]$ satisfies the q-Pascal identity $\binom{n+1}{d+1}_{q} = q^{d+1} \binom{n}{d+1}_{q} + \binom{n}{d}_{q}$, which reflects the Schubert cell stratification: either the chosen $d$-space contains a fixed $(d-1)$-space (giving $\binom{n}{d-1}_q$ choices after reduction) or it doesn't (giving $q^d \binom{n}{d}_q$ choices). The L-weighting by $q^{d+1}$ counts the affine cells.

title: Gaussian Binomial Identity: The Motivic Fibration Formula
content: Proves `gaussian_binomial_identity`: [Gr(d,n)] · [d]! · [n-d]! = [n]! for all d ≤ n. This is the motivic version of (n choose d) · d! · (n-d)! = n!. The inductive proof uses the q-Pascal recursion and the helper `geom_sum_split` lemma. Two key IH applications: (1) term1 uses IH with (d+1, n) to handle the L^{d+1} arm; (2) term2 uses IH with (d, n) and the q-factorial recurrence to handle the other arm. The final step applies `qNumber_split` to combine the two L-weighted terms.
mathContext: The identity $[\mathrm{Gr}(d,n)] \cdot [d]_{\mathbb{L}}! \cdot [n-d]_{\mathbb{L}}! = [n]_{\mathbb{L}}!$ has a geometric interpretation: the fibration $\mathrm{Fl}_n \to \mathrm{Gr}(d,n)$ with fiber $\mathrm{Fl}_d \times \mathrm{Fl}_{n-d}$ gives $[\mathrm{Fl}_n] = [\mathrm{Gr}(d,n)] \cdot [\mathrm{Fl}_d] \cdot [\mathrm{Fl}_{n-d}]$. Since $[\mathrm{Fl}_n] = [n]!$ and similarly for the fiber flags, this is exactly the Gaussian binomial identity.
prerequisites: induction on n with generalizing d

title: Grassmannian Duality: Lifting to Polynomial ℤ for Cancellation
content: Proves `grassmannianClass_duality`: [Gr(d,n)] = [Gr(n-d,n)] for all d ≤ n. The proof cannot cancel directly in a general commutative ring (no cancellation law). The elegant workaround: (1) define a specific `K0Var` instance over `Polynomial ℤ` with L := X, which IS an integral domain; (2) prove the duality in Polynomial ℤ by using the Gaussian binomial identity to show both sides equal [n]! and then cancel the nonzero q-factorial product via `mul_right_cancel₀`; (3) transfer back to K.carrier via the ring homomorphism `evalAtL` that evaluates X at K.L.
mathContext: The duality $[\mathrm{Gr}(d,n)] = [\mathrm{Gr}(n-d,n)]$ reflects the isomorphism $\mathrm{Gr}(d,n) \cong \mathrm{Gr}(n-d,n)$ given by $V \mapsto V^\perp$ (orthogonal complement). In K-theory, this is an equality of motivic classes. The proof strategy — lift to $\mathbb{Z}[X]$ (an integral domain), cancel, then evaluate — is a standard algebraic technique for extending identities from integral domains to general rings.

title: Partial Flag Varieties: Iterated Fibration Structure
content: Defines `PartialFlag n dims` as a structure of nested subspaces `V_{d₁} ⊂ ... ⊂ V_{dₖ} ⊂ kⁿ` with prescribed dimensions, and `partialFlagClass K n dims` via recursive iterated-Grassmannian product: for dims = [d₁,d₂,...], the class is [Gr(d₁,n)] · [Gr(d₂-d₁, n-d₁)] · ... Proved: `partialFlag_single`: Fl(d;n) = Gr(d,n); `complete_flag_is_partial_flag`: Fl_n = [n]!. These verify that the partial flag formula recovers known classes in the extremal cases.
mathContext: A **partial flag variety** $\mathrm{Fl}(d_1,\ldots,d_k;n)$ parameterizes chains $0 \subset V_1 \subset \cdots \subset V_k \subset k^n$ with $\dim V_i = d_i$. It admits an iterated fibration $\mathrm{Fl}(d_1,\ldots,d_k;n) \to \mathrm{Fl}(d_2,\ldots,d_k;n)$ with fiber $\mathrm{Gr}(d_1, d_2)$. Iterating: $[\mathrm{Fl}(d_1,\ldots,d_k;n)] = \prod_i [\mathrm{Gr}(d_{i+1} - d_i, n - d_i)]$ (where $d_0 = 0$).

title: Extension Conjecture: Parabolic Structure for Map Classes
content: Formalizes the core open conjecture as two axioms: (1) `motivicClassPartialFlagMaps`: the motivic class [Ω²_β(Fl(d₁,...,dₖ; n+1))] exists in K₀(Var); (2) `partial_flag_extension`: for positive β, this class equals [Levi × U × A^{a'}] where Levi = ∏GL_{nᵢ} is the Levi factor of the corresponding parabolic subgroup and U is the unipotent radical. The `unipotentDim` function computes dim(U) = ∑_{i<j} nᵢnⱼ where nᵢ are consecutive block sizes.
mathContext: The **parabolic subgroup** $P \subset \mathrm{GL}_n$ corresponding to a partial flag type is $P = L \ltimes U$ where $L = \mathrm{GL}_{n_1} \times \cdots \times \mathrm{GL}_{n_{k+1}}$ (Levi factor) and $U$ (unipotent radical) consists of block upper-triangular matrices with identity blocks. The conjecture $[\Omega^2_\beta \mathrm{Fl}(d_1,\ldots,d_k;n+1)] = [L \times U \times \mathbb{A}^{a'}]$ is the parabolic analog of Bryan et al.'s complete flag theorem $[\Omega^2_\beta \mathrm{Fl}_{n+1}] = [\mathrm{GL}_n \times \mathbb{A}^a]$.

title: GL_n = (L-1)^n · [Fl_n] · L^{T(n)}: The Structural Identity
content: Proves `GLn_qFactorial_decomposition`: [GL_n] = (L-1)^n · [n]_L! · L^{T(n)}, and `GLn_flag_relation`: [GL_n] = (L-1)^n · [Fl_n] · L^{T(n)}. The proof factorizes each (L^i - 1) via `geom_series_factor` as (L-1)·[i]_L, then uses `Finset.prod_mul_distrib` to separate the (L-1) factors from the q-number product. This structural identity is the algebraic explanation for why complete flag varieties appear in the GL_n formula: GL_n is built from Fl_n via a (L-1)^n-twisted bundle.
mathContext: The identity $[\mathrm{GL}_n] = (\mathbb{L}-1)^n \cdot [n]_{\mathbb{L}}! \cdot \mathbb{L}^{n(n-1)/2}$ follows from the **Bruhat decomposition**: $\mathrm{GL}_n = \bigsqcup_{w \in S_n} B w B$ where $B$ is the Borel subgroup. This gives $[\mathrm{GL}_n] = \sum_w \mathbb{L}^{\ell(w)} \cdot [B]^2 / [B]$. Since $[B] = (\mathbb{L}-1)^n \cdot \mathbb{L}^{n(n-1)/2}$ and $\sum_w \mathbb{L}^{\ell(w)} = [n]_{\mathbb{L}}!$ (the Poincaré polynomial of $S_n$), we get the formula.
